LESSON: WRITING 11.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.4: Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency
2. use synonyms and antonyms correctly in sentences

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 11.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING
This lesson teaches Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing for Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. use synonyms and antonyms correctly in sentences
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing above.
2. Explain Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words?
2. Which are some of the words with same or opposite meaning?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency
2. use synonyms and antonyms correctly in sentences

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
